articles.body: This is a submission for the Presage SmartSpectra SDK Challenge Status on Nov 19. The SDK measurements in this post were taken on my real webcam. The game itself has so far run end to end only on its simulator. My first real session and the demo video go in here before the deadline. Until then every picture below is from the simulator, and its banner says so. What I Built Feltbeat is a game with one instruction: sit still and count the heartbeats you can actually feel. No finger on your wrist. A webcam reads your pulse through the SmartSpectra SDK and keeps the real count to itself until you have typed yours. Then it shows you both. Your tally marks in ink, the camera's in red underneath. From the simulator. No number in this picture is a real reading.

articles.title: Kubernetes 1.33: What Really Breaks During an Upgrade and How to Anticipate It
articles.excerpt: Every cluster operator remembers Kubernetes 1.16 and 1.22: whole API groups disappeared overnight, Helm charts exploded, and kubectl apply started returning no matches for kind. Since then, teams buil…
articles.body: Every cluster operator remembers Kubernetes 1.16 and 1.22: whole API groups disappeared overnight, Helm charts exploded, and kubectl apply started returning no matches for kind . Since then, teams built reflexes around deprecated API scanning, and that is good. The problem with Kubernetes 1.33 is that those reflexes are no longer sufficient. 1.33 removes no major GA API. If your upgrade plan is "run pluto , see zero removed APIs, click upgrade", you will pass the audit and still break the cluster — because in 1.33 the breakage moved to three other places: feature gates that no longer exist , kubelet default behaviour changes , and aggregated APIService endpoints that silently rot .
articles.author: Florient DOGBE

articles.title: The Myth of the Page Fault: Minor vs Major Faults in Linux
articles.excerpt: The Myth of the Page Fault: Minor vs Major Faults in Linux Ask most software engineers what happens during a Page Fault, and the textbook answer is immediate: "The requested memory address is missing…
articles.body: The Myth of the Page Fault: Minor vs Major Faults in Linux Ask most software engineers what happens during a Page Fault , and the textbook answer is immediate: "The requested memory address is missing from RAM, so the operating system suspends the process and reads the page from the hard drive or swap partition." While this describes a Major (Hard) Page Fault , it represents a tiny minority of real-world events. In production Linux systems, over 95% of all page faults involve zero disk I/O . They are Minor (Soft) Page Faults . 1. The Hardware Definition of a Page Fault A Page Fault is not a storage subsystem command. It is a CPU architectural interrupt (Interrupt 14 on x86-64).
articles.author: Binary Dose

articles.title: Your SVG optimizer silently broke your icon. Here's the one-line check.
articles.excerpt: Your SVG optimizer silently broke your icon. Here's the one-line check. I spent an afternoon comparing SVG optimizers on a set of 28 real icons from Simple Icons. The sizes looked fine. Two files made…
articles.body: Your SVG optimizer silently broke your icon. Here's the one-line check. I spent an afternoon comparing SVG optimizers on a set of 28 real icons from Simple Icons. The sizes looked fine. Two files made the batch tool crash. Three of them produced a file that opened without complaint, rendered as a blank square, and reported a smaller byte count than the original. The reason: the optimizer had replaced path coordinates with the literal string NaN . This post is what I learned about the failure, how to detect it in one command, and why a preview can show you a perfect icon while the file you download is broken. What NaN in a path means A <path d="..."> is a list of drawing commands followed by numbers.

articles.title: StatefulSet and CSI: Resizing a Production Volume Without Losing a Single Byte
articles.excerpt: Every StatefulSet eventually hits the same wall: the 50 Gi volume you provisioned eighteen months ago for a PostgreSQL replica is at 92 %, the WAL is growing, and the on-call rotation is getting alert…
articles.body: Every StatefulSet eventually hits the same wall: the 50 Gi volume you provisioned eighteen months ago for a PostgreSQL replica is at 92 %, the WAL is growing, and the on-call rotation is getting alerts at 03:00. The good news is that the CSI spec has supported online volume expansion for years. The bad news is that StatefulSet.spec.volumeClaimTemplates is immutable, so the obvious kubectl edit fails with a validation error and people start improvising — which is how data gets lost. This article walks through the real procedure: what actually happens under the hood when you grow a PVC, how to work around the immutable volumeClaimTemplates field with an orchestrated recreation, and — the part most runbooks skip — how to prove that the filesystem inside the pod actually grew.
articles.author: Florient DOGBE

articles.title: Coroutines first: notes on nRouter's Kotlin SDK
articles.excerpt: A Kotlin client for an API gateway can be a thin wrapper around blocking HTTP calls, with a coroutine adapter bolted on. The nRouter Kotlin guide goes the other way: the SDK is coroutines-first from t…
articles.body: A Kotlin client for an API gateway can be a thin wrapper around blocking HTTP calls, with a coroutine adapter bolted on. The nRouter Kotlin guide goes the other way: the SDK is coroutines-first from the start — suspend functions for calls, a cold Flow for streaming, and typed error subclasses you can branch on. Full guide: https://nrouter.ai/docs/sdks/kotlin Setup The guide publishes the artifact to your local Maven cache ( ./gradlew clean check publishToMavenLocal ), then it's a normal Gradle dependency: dependencies { implementation ( "ai.nrouter:nrouter-sdk-kotlin:3.1.2" ) } NRouter() reads NROUTER_API_KEY from the environment, targets https://api.nrouter.ai/v1 , and dispatches on Dispatchers.IO , so calls don't block your caller's context.

articles.excerpt: The Voyager 1 probe continues to fly out into interstellar space after its historic distance milestone. NASA expects it to keep working until at least 2027.
articles.body: Voyager 1 has reached a historic milestone in space — it now takes a light-day to send a command to the spacecraft, meaning a full 24 hours for Earth to hail the distant spacecraft. Since Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2 , launched on an initial tour through the outer solar system in 1977, their missions have been packed with science. Voyager 1 looked at Jupiter and Saturn from up close before veering for a flyby of Saturn's moon Titan and Saturn's rings, a pathway that brought it above the plane of the solar system in the early 1980s. Voyager 1's faster path out of the solar system brought it to one light-day in distance on Wednesday (Nov. 18), while Voyager 2 — which took a slightly slower track to see Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune — will reach a light-day of distance in 2035.

The brightest star, left of the center, is blue Alnitak (the Girdle): a triple star system best known for being the easternmost star in Orion’s Belt . The instantly recognizable shape of a dark horse’s head at the center is the aptly named Horsehead Nebula .

articles.body: NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 24 mission launched Saturday, April 11, 2026, aboard the company’s Cygnus XL spacecraft atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission will deliver approximately 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station. Credit: Northrop Grumman NASA, Northrop Grumman, and SpaceX are targeting no earlier than 10:47 a.m. EST, Sunday, Nov. 29, for the next launch delivering science investigations, supplies, and equipment to the International Space Station. The agency also will hold a prelaunch media teleconference on Monday, Nov. 23.
